subject: ENGLISH
title: Digraph Detectives · M01 D14
objective: Recognize taught ch and sh digraphs.
introduction: Ch and sh are two letters that make one sound. Be a detective and spot them in words like chair and ship!

vocabulary.definition: Two letters that make one sound, like sh or ch.
What you hear when someone says a word; ch and sh are examples.
A clue hunter; your job is to find ch and sh in words.

activities.instruction: Learn how ch and sh make one sound with two letters!
activities.content: In the taught words, ch or sh uses two letters to represent one main sound. English has exceptions, so use the lesson examples.

feedback.retry: Look for ch or sh: two letters representing one main sound in these words. 💪

activities.accessibilityAlternative: Text alternative: In the taught words, ch or sh uses two letters to represent one main sound. English has exceptions, so use the lesson examples.

items.explanation: Chair has ch: two letters that make one sound. Stop and flag begin with blends, where you can hear two sounds.

items.prompt: Which word contains a common digraph?
items.explanation: Chair contains ch, two letters that make one sound. Stop and flag have blends at the start, not digraphs.

items.prompt: Which word does NOT have a digraph?
items.explanation: Stop has no digraph: st is a blend with two sounds. Chair and chop both have ch.
Ship begins with sh — two letters, one /sh/ sound. Stop begins with st, and chair begins with ch.

items.prompt: Which word begins with ch or sh?
items.explanation: Ship begins with sh, so it starts with a digraph. Nest begins with n, and stop begins with st.
